systems.name: Structure & floors
systems.description: A concrete frame around a generous central void.

assemblies.name: Street edges, wells & access bridges
assemblies.description: Granite paving, railings and bridges separate the building from the surrounding streets.
assemblies.significance: A simplified ground-level setting makes the exposed base and points of arrival easier to read.

assemblies.name: Concrete columns & capitals
assemblies.description: Columns and beams support the galleries around the atrium.
assemblies.significance: The visible frame gives the large interior a legible structure.

assemblies.name: External cross-bracing
assemblies.description: Diagonal members articulate the outside of the frame.
assemblies.significance: Their position expresses how the building is supported.

systems.name: Façade & glazing
systems.description: Repeated glazed bays and an exposed structural rhythm.

assemblies.name: Glazed façade bays
assemblies.description: The glazing forms a layered environmental envelope.
assemblies.significance: The original design used the glazing as part of the air-handling strategy. Panels here simplify that construction.

assemblies.name: Mullions & maintenance galleries
assemblies.description: A repeating grid gives the elevations their fine grain.
assemblies.significance: Visible rails and frames help reveal the building’s many layers.

systems.name: Service towers
systems.description: Six perimeter towers make the building’s workings visible.

assemblies.name: Leadenhall Place meeting pods
assemblies.description: Stacked meeting-room enclosures articulate the Leadenhall Place end.
assemblies.significance: These broader pods are distinct from the service cabins; their interiors are not reproduced.

assemblies.name: Ground-level air intakes
assemblies.description: A row of seven cylindrical intakes stands outside the south-west corner.
assemblies.significance: The exposed services continue all the way down to ground level. Positions and terminations are simplified.

assemblies.name: North-west service tower
assemblies.description: Perimeter towers accommodate the building’s services.
assemblies.significance: Keeping services outside frees up the interior. These positional names are model labels, not official tower designations.

assemblies.name: Prefabricated service pods
assemblies.description: Projecting rectangular service enclosures sit beside the curved stairs.
assemblies.significance: Individual pods, portholes and their supporting framework are interpreted from the supplied close-up references; their internal fit-out is not modelled.

assemblies.name: Exposed ducts & risers
assemblies.description: External pipes make servicing visible and accessible.
assemblies.significance: Routes are simplified from photographs, not an engineering services survey.

assemblies.name: Rooftop plant rooms
assemblies.description: Four large steel-clad plant rooms crown the taller service towers.
assemblies.significance: Their varied heights contribute to the distinctive silhouette.

systems.name: Lifts, stairs & escalators
systems.description: External vertical routes and interior connections.

assemblies.name: Vaulted entrance canopy
assemblies.description: A small glazed vault marks an entrance at the base of the service towers.
assemblies.significance: The canopy repeats the architectural language of the central roof at street scale.

assemblies.name: External glass lifts
assemblies.description: Lloyd’s has twelve external glass lifts.
assemblies.significance: Glazed lift cars turn movement into part of the elevation. This model uses representative positions.

assemblies.name: Stainless-steel stair enclosures
assemblies.description: Stairs provide routes between levels at the perimeter.
assemblies.significance: Stacked curved enclosures are a signature of the inside-out architecture.

assemblies.name: Central escalators
assemblies.description: Escalators link the lower trading levels across the atrium.
assemblies.significance: Their open arrangement makes movement between galleries visible. Routes and step counts are illustrative.

systems.name: Atrium & roof
systems.description: A glass vault above the central space.

assemblies.name: Barrel-vaulted glass roof
assemblies.description: The steel-and-glass vault brings daylight into the atrium.
assemblies.significance: A light lattice spans above the heavier concrete structure.

assemblies.name: Atrium end screens
assemblies.description: Tall glazed ends continue the roof’s slender framework.
assemblies.significance: These simplified screens reveal the vertical extent of the atrium.

assemblies.name: Blue maintenance cranes
assemblies.description: Permanent rooftop cranes support exterior maintenance.
assemblies.significance: They make the building’s continued care visible on its skyline.

systems.name: Underwriting Room
systems.description: An illustrative setting for face-to-face negotiation.

assemblies.name: Representative underwriting boxes
assemblies.description: Brokers meet underwriters at desks known as boxes.
assemblies.significance: These invented furnishings explain the use of the space. They do not show current desk allocations.

assemblies.name: Coffered lighting grid
assemblies.description: Ceiling lights in the building also serve as air extractors.
assemblies.significance: The model suggests the ceiling rhythm without reproducing its technical details.

systems.name: Heritage features
systems.description: Historic objects within a modern architectural setting.

assemblies.name: Retained Cooper entrance
assemblies.description: The stone entrance screen survives from Sir Edwin Cooper’s earlier Lloyd’s building on Leadenhall Street.
assemblies.significance: A restrained interpretation of the arch, pediment and stonework; sculptural ornament and exact placement are not reproduced.

assemblies.name: The Rostrum & Lutine Bell
assemblies.description: The mahogany Rostrum holds the historic Lutine Bell.
assemblies.significance: This simplified representation marks a link between the market’s history and its modern home.
